content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having trouble controlling a [product_name] VFD using [product_name] and the [product_name] as a bridge. I followed the [company_name] application example found at [url], but I can't get it to work. My setup uses [product_name] software version [version_no], and I've downloaded the program to the module. The program example from the article and the CCF file were uploaded to the [product_name]. The S7 connection between the module and [product_name] seems functional, as I can see the control word changing when using the web interface. However, the status word values and status indicators on the website do not update, except for "reverse" and "ack". I suspect the main issue is the Modbus RTU connection between [product_name] and the VFD. My goal is to be able to start/stop and adjust the frequency of the VFD through the web page. This is my first try with BUS control, so any basic advice would be appreciated.

Hello, I recently used this example for a project and extended it for my application. Which browser are you working with? It seemed browser choice didn't matter, but for some reason, it only worked properly for me when using Mozilla Firefox. Best regards, [user_name].

Hi, sorry for my delayed response. I doubt the browser is the problem—information transfers via the [product_name] web interface to the [product_name] program without issue. It looks like the issue is specifically between the [product_name] and the [product_name] VFD.
I reconstructed the project and noticed it doesn't work well with Google Chrome, but it worked immediately with Mozilla Firefox.
Hi, If you've already tried using Firefox, the only other suggestion I have is to double check the polarity and wiring connections for your RTU wires.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are attempting to control a [product_name] VFD using [product_name] modules, experiencing communication issues between the bridge module and the VFD over Modbus RTU. While the web interface and [product_name] configuration show partial success, the main obstacle appears to be the hardware connection and Modbus RTU communication, not browser compatibility. However, several contributors report browser-specific quirks when interacting with the web interface, with Mozilla Firefox being the most reliable. Overall, hardware connections and browser choice both lead to troubleshooting challenges for those new to BUS control setups.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate a simple configuration process and dependable operation for controlling the VFD via the bridge module and web interface—including clear start/stop and frequency control with accurate status feedback and minimal troubleshooting required.
